articles.title: Jensen Huang isn’t out of the woods yet
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.content:
It’s safe to say no one expectedthis.

Monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services. With so much of the AI industry built on top of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, Huang’s departure looked like an imminent threat to the business — and the mood on his return has been ecstatic. Share prices are rocketing back up, particularly for neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7% on the news.

Still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement. President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning.

Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it. Among Jensen Huang’s defenders, it’s become common to question whether Alice Huang was really a spy, but it’s clear that a lot of restricted chips were flowing into China through her company. Just this weekend,The New York Times reportedsustained contact between Alice Huang and a member of China’s Ministry of State Security during the same period she was having an affair with Jensen Huang.

With Democrats in control of Congress, including investigative bodies like the House Oversight Committee, there are plenty of ways to force the issue. Nvidia’s role in violating U.S. export controls would likely have been the subject of prolonged uncomfortable investigation, whether Huang returned or not. But with him back in the CEO’s seat, there will be a lot more riding on any revelations that come up — and any new revelations will damage Nvidia as a company alongside Huang himself.

Then there are the questions raised by Trump’s intervention. It’s unprecedented in American history for a sitting president to intervene to clear a CEO accused of being a national security risk. Simply pressing the Department of Justice to exonerate Huang would have been a scandal, butcalling the Nvidia boardgoes significantly further. Huang has alreadydonated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project, so it’s easy to make the case that Trump was intervening on behalf of a donor, setting national security risks aside for his personal benefit.

All of this is happening just as Democrats retake Congress, with all of its associated investigative powers. Even if they can’t fire Huang or remove Trump, there are lots of uncomfortable questions that are still unanswered. Was there any Department of Justice inquiry into whether Huang had committed a crime, or did Trump make the call on his own? Did the intelligence services make any official assessment that could be subpoenaed into the congressional record? Investigating Democrats will be particularly interested in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees export controls andretains significant financial ties to the industrythrough his firm, Cantor Fitzgerald.

If all of this sounds exhausting, you’re getting a sense of what the next year will be like for anyone following national news. Congress will keep a steady drip of embarrassing revelations, milking as much political juice as possible out of Huang and everyone associated with him. Trump will keep lashing out, often making things worse for everyone involved. (Trump’sstatement to CBS, which defends Huang in racist terms while also accusing him of treason, is an early taste.) It’s going to be ugly and sad, and the most successful tech company of the last decade will be right at the center of it.

I have to assume that this was the scenario the board was concerned about when it decided to remove Huang two weeks ago. Since then, the cost of removing him has gone up: an open letter from Nvidia’s employees and partners, a tanking stock market, and, ultimately, direct intervention from the president of the United States.

But nothing has lowered the cost of keeping Huang, and the ugly scenario the board foresaw earlier this month is still very much in place. We’re about to see it come to life.

articles.title: Trump reportedly called into Nvidia board meeting to advocate for Huang’s return
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.content:
A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trumpreportedlydialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’sreinstatementshortly afterward.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the presidenttoldCNBC.

Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he hadaffairswith an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, toremarkthat “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.”

According to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

While Trump hasdeclaredthat Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet.

“People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said to CNBC.

Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, evendenyingthat he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Timesreported, on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May.

Earlier this spring, Rubio alsosupervisedthe drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security.

articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.content:
Enterprise customer experience companySierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, whichvalued the company at $15 billion.

The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to$400 million within five months.

That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which iscreating a platform to build agents and partnerwith model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working oncreating protocol definitionsfor agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

Startups operating in the CX space have seen multimillion-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion;Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion;Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; andParloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.

During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec
articles.content:
In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s boardsaidon Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after heresignedfollowing his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.

The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.

Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.

In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.

Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whomsigned a petitionpushing for reinstatement.

The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”

Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”

In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

articles.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
articles.author: Zack Whittaker
articles.content:
Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike hasagreed to buy Zscalerin a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies announced Monday.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler said that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era.

Zscaler is a San Jose, California-based tech company that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network.

CrowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones, and other devices connected to a company’s network, said the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers.

In remarks on Monday, the companies said that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI.

The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year.

articles.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.content:
President TrumppraisedNvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”

The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.

In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.

There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board.Speaking to a PBS journalistover the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”

Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.

Trumpsaid last weekthat he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”

Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

articles.title: The best apps to make new friends right now
articles.author: Lauren Forristal
articles.content:
In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent.

In 2023, theU.S. Surgeon Generalwent so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships.

Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities.

According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025.

The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations.

From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships. We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out.

The app222is aniOS-onlysocial events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results.The appsends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one.

The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price.

Dating giantBumbleis among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching itsfriend-finding featurein 2016, which then spun out into astand-alone appin 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone asignificant redesign, with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles.

BFF is available for free download oniOSandAndroiddevices.

Clyxis anotheremerging appin the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events.

As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list. The app is available on theApp StoreandGoogle Play Store.

Crowdieris a new group social app that lets friend groups connect with others. Users can create a group of two-five friends and browse other groups to arrange hangouts in person.

To initiate a match, users can “Wave” at groups they like, and if those groups wave back, they can plan in a shared chat. A match requires the majority of both groups to agree. For example, two people in a four-person group need to say yes.

The app is available for free oniOSandAndroiddevices.

Les Amísis afriendship apptailored for women, transgender, and LGBTQ+ individuals that leverages AI to match users based on similar interests and encourages participation in local events, such as pottery classes, book clubs, and wine tastings. Matches are made every Monday, allowing users to chat and plan meetups later in the week.

Available oniOSandAndroid, Les Amís serves cities across Europe, including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and Stockholm. In the U.S., the app is available in Austin and New York, with plans to expand to Boston, Miami, and Los Angeles.

The app uses a paid membership model that varies by city, with fees of $70 in New York and €55 in Amsterdam.

Thelocal event-discovery platformhas been around since 2002, helping millions of users connect with others who share similar interests. Users can RSVP to events; join groups that cater to a variety of hobbies, professions, or social causes; and create their own groups and events. They can also chat with group members and post updates and photos from gatherings.

This Europeancommunity-building apprecently launched in the U.S., targeting users over 40 who want to meet new people in their area and participate in group activities such as picnics, concerts, and hiking. Notably, in a short time, there have been around 777,000 U.S. downloads so far across theApp StoreandGoogle Play Store, according to Appfigures estimates.

Pieis another one of the newersocial appson the market. It features an AI-driven quiz designed to predict which users are most likely to be compatible with each other. Each person who RSVPs to a Pie event takes a brief personality assessment, and the algorithm organizes attendees into groups of six, who are then added to a group chat within the Pie app, allowing them to interact with each other before the event.

Currently, the app is only available in Austin, Chicago, and San Francisco. Users can download Pie from theApp StoreandGoogle Play Store.

Timeleftis a relatively new platform that helps you organize weekly dinner dates with groups of strangers. The app uses a special algorithm to match you with others, taking into account your age, gender, and personality. Users are matched with four other people, but they only learn minor details about them the night before, including their occupations and zodiac signs.

Dinners take place at a selected restaurant on Wednesday evenings at 7:00 p.m. To help everyone break the ice, the app offers a game with conversation starters. After dinner, there is an after-party at a local bar.

Users can book dinners online or through theapp. In terms of pricing, it varies depending on the country and restaurant. Users pay for a ticket up front and are responsible for covering their own dinner and drinks.

Washed Upis a social event discovery app that launched in early 2026, designed for people in the Los Angeles area who want an easier way to find things to do and meet new people.

The app helps users discover local events, such as concerts, trivia nights, and comedy shows, while also giving them a built-in way to connect with others who plan to attend. Instead of going to events alone, users can create or join “plans,” which are small group meetups tied to specific events. Users can browse these plans and request to join, chat with the group, and add new friends, making it easier to show up to events with people rather than by themselves.

It’s available to download onthe App Store.

Wyzr Friendsis anactivity-based friendship appdesigned for adults 40 and older, catering to empty nesters, those who are divorced, and other users seeking to connect with like-minded individuals. Users can thumbs up or down potential friends and arrange in-person activities based on shared interests, such as going to the movies or hiking.

It’s available oniOSandAndroiddevices in the U.S., Canada, Australia, Ireland, the Philippines, Singapore, and Mexico.

Mmotionis anewly launchedfriendship app that blends location tracking with social discovery to help users connect with people nearby and explore new bars and restaurants in their area. Upon joining, users can participate in interest-based groups — such as hiking, basketball, or art — view a map of active users, and send messages to those nearby. The app also highlights new places on the map, making it easy to find a restaurant or venue to try.

Mmotion is currently only available to users in New York City oniOSand Android devices. Users must first submit an application to be considered.

Launched in March 2026,Synchronyis a new social app tailored for neurodivergent adults. Founded by a mother of a son on the autism spectrum, it aims to create a supportive community through features like interest-based matching and two-step identity verification. This ensures that users engage safely, as both a user and a trusted person must verify personal details and a photo ID during registration.

A standout feature is Jesse, an optional AI communication tool that assists users in navigating conversations. The AI provides editable prompts to help express thoughts, clarifies conversations, and offers boundary-setting suggestions. While the incorporation of AI may raise concerns, there are guardrails built into Jesse, such as avoiding medical advice.

Users must pay a monthly subscription of $44.99 after a 30-day free trial. It’s available oniOSandAndroiddevices.

This story was updated after publication.

articles.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
articles.author: Marina Temkin
articles.content:
When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.

But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its2024 splitfrom its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.

“We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.

Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said.

Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised$81.3 billionin the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.

Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win.

Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.

“Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.

Lillian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.

After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said.

“It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations.

articles.title: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.content:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amida series of scandals— including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and aninterventionby President Donald Trump.

After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.

“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, hadsigned an open letteradvocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders alsopushedfor Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”

Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Timesreportedthat Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

articles.title: ‘Outrageous,’ ‘reckless,’ ‘wow’: Here’s what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.content:
Jensen Huangis back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance witha suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world,has now been reinstatedby the company’s board. The move was one thatPresident Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the president postedan AI-generated memeof the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled thefamous photofrom Trump’s own assassination attempt.

Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affairwith Alice Huangmay have exposed the company.

Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder mayface an uphill battlegiven the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting witha public Senate appearance scheduledfor next week. He isalso expectedto testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.
